articles.title: Today’s Top Deals: PS5 SSDs, Xbox and Nintendo Gift Cards, and LEGO Star Wars
articles.summary: Plus, don’t miss discounts on gaming PCs, physical Switch games, and more.
articles.body:
It’s officially Fall, and that means we’re only a couple of weeks away from Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days and a couple of months away from Black Friday . But if you don’t want to wait that long, incredible deals on gaming PCs, PS5 SSDs, and more are happening today. We’re also in the final few days of the Nintendo Customer Appreciation Sale , so be sure to pick up all the discounted physical Switch games .

Verbatim 1TB Vi7000 PCIe NVMe M.2 2280 Internal SSD

Verbatim 2TB Vi7000 PCIe NVMe M.2 2280 Internal SSD

Acer Nitro 85 AMD Ryzen 7 8700F RTX 5070 Gaming PC (16GB/1TB)

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Pitch Black Elite Trainer Box

Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 - Switch

Bookcessories: Tiny Book of Winnie the Pooh

PNY NVIDIA GeForce RTX™ 5070 OC Triple Fan 12GB GDDR7, SFF-Ready, 2.4-Slot

Legion Go S Ryzen Z1 Extreme/SteamOS (32GB/1TB)

LEGO Sonic the Hedgehog Sonic: Speedster Lightning

Xbox Wireless Controller + $50 Xbox Gift Card Bundle

Take a scroll through today's top discounts, and find out more below:

SSD prices keep skyrocketing, but if you’re after some semblance of a deal, grab either the Verbatim 1TB or 2TB SSD at Walmart. These PS5-compatible PCIe Gen4 x4 SSDs with an M.2 2280 form factor already have an aluminum heatsink installed, a must for the PS5’s toasty slot. Both also far exceed the minimum sequential read speed requirements of the console, hitting up to 7,000MB/s. For added peace of mind, it looks like a 2-year limited warranty even comes with both drives.

$170 in Nintendo eShop Gift Cards for $150

When you buy a $150 Nintendo eShop Gift Card on Newegg, you get a bonus $20 eShop Gift Card, no code needed. While you can use these gift cards to buy digital games, DLC, online memberships, and in-game currency in the eShop, those funds can be added to your account to purchase hardware and physical games from the Nintendo Store, too. If you’re looking to pick up anything from Nintendo, it’s an incredible way to save. Maybe you even want to grab the new Switch 2 + Mario Kart World bundle ?

The Nintendo eShop Gift Card isn’t the only gift card deal on Newegg. You can also snag a $100 Xbox Gift Card, which includes a $15 Xbox Gift Card while supplies last. After you receive it and add it to your Microsoft account, it can be used to buy games, apps, DLC, hardware, accessories, subscriptions, and more. It’s not just for Xbox either; it works at the Microsoft Store and Windows. If you haven’t picked up the GTA VI preorder, it’s also one way to save.

Save $24 on the LEGO U-Wing Star Fighter

Pick up a LEGO U-Wing Star Fighter for just $45.99 at Kohl’s. All you need is a free Kohl’s Rewards Account and the code TOYS10 to get an extra $10 off $50, and yes, this code works on LEGO. If you have a Kohl’s near you where you can pick up the order, you’ll get an extra $5 off. Be sure to check out more LEGO sets on sale here . As for the U-Wing Star Fighter, it features 594 pieces, four mini-figures, and the iconic ship complete with the distinctive 'V' formation flight mode.

LEGO Star Wars SMART Play: Millennium Falcon (#75426)

Save $500 on Acer Nitro 85 RTX 5070 and More Discounted Gaming PCs

It’s GeForce Week at Walmart, and that means a whole bunch of gaming PCs have received solid discounts, including the Acer Nitro 85 RTX 5070 . It’s down $500 to $1,399. The GPU alone is going for $700 or more these days. Then add the AMD Ryzen 7 8700F CPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB M.2 SSD, and you’ve got a killer 1080p and 1440p gaming PC.

Of course, that’s not the only gaming PC deal; check out even more highlights from the sale below:

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution Pitch Black ETB Restocked on Amazon

The Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution Pitch Black Elite Trainer Box is back in stock on Amazon and going for $77.37. Is it at MSRP? No, but it’s right around market value, shipped and sold by Amazon. Inside the box are 9 Boosters, a full-art foil promo card featuring Zarude, 65 card sleeves, 40 Pokémon TCG Energy cards, a player’s guide, and more.

Super Mario Galaxy for $49 and More Physical Switch Game Deals

A game cartridge of Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 for Switch is still down to $49 for Nintendo’s Customer Appreciation Sale . With this game package, you are essentially getting two for the price of one. Both Super Mario Galaxy and Super Mario Galaxy 2 received rave reviews when they first launched on the Wii. These updated versions add UI improvements, a new in-game music player, and the ability to play using buttons and sticks or motion controls. There’s also a boosted resolution that goes up to 4K on Switch 2 with a free update, while Rosalina's in-game storybook has some interesting new pages.

That’s not the only physical Switch game deal worth grabbing. Below are a few more top options to consider adding to your collection:

Disney and Star Wars Bookcessories Already Discounted

A new Disney Bookcessories collection from Insight Edition just launched and is already discounted on Amazon. Part tiny book and part matching themed key chain case, these adorable little accessories are designed to go with you anywhere. The books measure just 1.34” x 1.73” but still feature images, quotes, and more, while the character book case is made of durable PVC and comes with a clip. Right now, you can pick up three Star Wars-themed and six Disney-themed bookcessories. Below are all the available options:

PNY Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 OC 12GB GDDR7 GPU for $679

Walmart has a PNY Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 OC 12GB GDDR7 GPU for $679. Admittedly, calling this a deal is a bit of a stretch since it’s well above MSRP, but it’s one of the best prices on a GeForce RTX 5070 in the current market. This midrange GPU offers solid performance gains over its predecessor, especially with the DLSS 4 support. It’s an excellent option for high-frame-rate 1440p and 1080p gaming. Read IGN’s full review to find out more. You can also pick up the PNY Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti OC 16GB GDDR7 for $999 , which is the best deal I’ve found on that GPU in a while.

Get 7 Games for $15 with IGN Humble Bundle

IGN has its own Humble Bundle to celebrate our 30th anniversary, and it’s now live. For just $15, this collection includes a bunch of heavy hitters, from The Elder Scrolls Online - Elsweyr to Remnant II. You also get BlazBlue Entropy Effect, Ravenswatch, Subnautica, Thronebreaker: The Witcher Tales, and Sonic Adventure 2. That’s a total of seven games, and all are easily redeemable on Steam.

Save Almost $800 on a Lenovo Legion Go S - Ryzen Z1 Extreme (SteamOS)

The Lenovo Legion Go S unfortunately got a serious price hike a few months ago. However, you can pick up an Open Box - Excellent condition AMD Ryzen Z1 Extreme and SteamOS model with 32GB of RAM and 1TB SSD for just $800. A new one is also available for $999.99 , still over $500 off its current list price. This particular model is a top SteamOS handheld gaming PC , and IGN’s PC hardware expert Jackie Thomas even gave it an “Amazing” 9/10 rating in her review . With the Steam Deck seeing a massive price increase and limited availability, it’s an incredible alternative.

Pay Just $6 for Hogwarts Legacy on Switch

A digital version of Hogwarts Legacy for Switch is down to just $5.99 on Nintendo. Sure, it may struggle a bit on the Switch, but the open-world RPG plays exceptionally well on the Switch 2, especially if you buy the $10 upgrade pack after you own it. Scoring an “Amazing” 9/10 in IGN’s review , Travis Northup found that Hogwarts Legacy “captures all the excitement and wonder of the Wizarding World with its memorable new characters, challenging and nuanced combat, and a wonderfully executed Hogwarts student fantasy that kept me glued to my controller for dozens of hours.” For $6, there’s not much to lose.

You can also pick up digital Switch 2 versions of Final Fantasy games cheaply at Nintendo right now. Check them out below:

FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE INTERGRADE - Switch 2

FINAL FANTASY X/X-2 HD Remaster - Switch 2

FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles - Switch 2

Get 26% Off a Silent Hill: Townfall Steam Code

The latest in the Silent Hill franchise, Townfall, is out this week, just in time for spooky season. If you’re looking to play it on PC, a Steam code from Fanatical is 25% off. IGN has already posted the review , giving it a “Great” 8/10 rating. Reviewer Tristan Ogilvie found: “Silent Hill: Townfall feels like Konami’s seminal survival horror series returning to what it does best. Its atmosphere is oppressively ominous, its central mystery is genuinely compelling to unravel and packed with themes that feel fresh, and its army of disfigured demons is exhilarating to both encounter and evade.

Xbox Wireless Controller + $50 Xbox Gift Card Bundle for $80

Score IGN’s top PC controller , the Xbox Wireless Controller, and a $50 Xbox Gift Card for just $79.99 on Newegg. That essentially makes the controller just $29.99. It’s the same controller that comes bundled with the XSX and features a familiar design, a responsive D-pad, a 3.5mm audio jack, a textured grip, and simple button mapping in the Xbox app. Expect a seamless wireless connection to the console or PC via Bluetooth, or a wired USB-C connection. As for the gift card, it gets added to your Microsoft account for purchasing games, apps, DLC, hardware, subscriptions, and more from the Microsoft Store, Windows, and Xbox. You can even use it towards a Grand Theft Auto VI preorder .

Danielle is a Tech freelance writer based in Los Angeles who spends her free time creating videos and geeking out over music history.

articles.title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls PC Sales Figures and Player Count Spark Worry From Players About Game's Longevity
articles.summary: It’s been over a month since Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls released, and its early sales figures and player counts on PC are sparking concern within the fighting game community about its longevity.
articles.body:
It’s been over a month since Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls released, and its early sales figures and player counts on PC are sparking concern within the fighting game community about its longevity.

Arc System Works’ latest tag fighting game has suffered no end of discourse within the FGC; some players love it, while others are severely dissatisfied with its tag system and online matchmaking, and it’s almost impossible to avoid this debate if you’re on fighting game Twitter right now. Most everyone was excited for a new, fast-paced Marvel fighting game from the developers of the highly-lauded Guilty Gear series and Dragon Ball FighterZ — but after launch, that excitement seems to have dwindled into a spiral of frustration.

Data from Steam Charts shows that the title boasts a current active PC player count of 427 players on Steam, with a 24-hour peak of 791 players. The game’s all-time peak on Steam is listed at 13,787 players, but keep in mind that these are just Steam figures and don’t account for PlayStation users.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Knights of Doom State of Play June 2026 Reveal Trailer - Screenshots

Sales figures for Tokon on PC have also driven discourse around the game; data from Alinea Analytics shows a cavernous disparity between platforms, with 82% of copies being sold on PlayStation compared to just 18% on Steam. That being said, it has generated an estimated $49.7 million in revenue, selling approximately 750,000 copies across both platforms combined.

Those numbers aren’t anything to sniff at, and it’s worth noting that the competition is stiff. Street Fighter 6 is definitely the most successful fighting game on the market right now, and Tokon was unlikely to ever topple it. The game is certainly seeing success on PlayStation — but its extremely rough launch on PC is likely to blame for the severe disparity between who's playing on what platform.

The game infamously suffered issues with its PC port at launch, to the point where prominent community figure Maximilian Dood literally uninstalled it during one of his live streams in a damning moment that went viral. While a patch was quickly released to help solve these problems, Tokon’s producer admitted that it would be difficult to regain players’ trust after this, and the game’s director, Kazuto Sekine, apologized for the ordeal in an honest statement a month later.

While Tokon appears to be thriving on PlayStation, its comparatively lackluster playerbase on PC and strikingly smaller sales figures on Steam have sparked a debate within the fighting game community as to whether or not the game has what it takes to weather the storm in an increasingly crowded market of IP-based tag fighting games (hello, Invincible VS and Avatar Legends). We also can’t discount the fact that the game was initially blocked in 132 countries due to PSN requirements.

One of the loudest voices in this conversation is Guilty Gear and Smash Bros pro William ‘Leffen’ Hjelte. “Unless Tokon turns the game around gameplay wise by next patch, I'm gonna drop it,” he wrote in a viral post on X/Twitter. “Gameplay aside, I can't even get matches in EU, it feels like the serious playerbase is maybe, at best, 1/10th of Strive’s and 2XKO’s here.

“I genuinely think the game is saveable if they act fast and correctly, but with us not even knowing when the patch is coming and only four characters coming (no date), I think it's probably over, at least if you care about having a big scene. Very sad, I had a lot of high hopes for Tokon.”

I genuinely think the game is saveable if they act fast and correctly but with us not even knowing when the patch is coming and only 4 chars coming (no date) I think its probably over, at least if you care about having a big scene. Very sad, I had a lot of high hopes for Tokon. — Leffen (@TSM_Leffen) September 22, 2026

I genuinely think the game is saveable if they act fast and correctly but with us not even knowing when the patch is coming and only 4 chars coming (no date) I think its probably over, at least if you care about having a big scene. Very sad, I had a lot of high hopes for Tokon.

“Dragon Ball FighterZ sold over two million copies in its first week,” another player pointed out. “Tokon probably won't even break one million in six months. This is truly sad that they fumbled such an easy win.”

“Yeah... This game will only have a year's worth of content, and only because it's already made or in the planning stages. I don't think Cyclops will bring in the crowd Tokon needs,” another speculated .

Others, however, are arguing that it’s only been just under two months since the game came out, and are pointing to its success on PlayStation as to why things might not be as grim as some voices in the FGC believe.

“Marvel Tokon came out August 6. Not even two months ago,” YouTuber and prominent community member Mightykeef said. “Not… even… two months ago. I’ve seen such an insane amount of doom posting for a fighting game that has not even been able to breath for two months, lol.”

“Tokon is an incredible fighting game, but it's still a fighting game. Always a niche genre. Hell, one of the goats of the genre, UMVC3, didn't crack 600k in two months,” another pointed out .

“It took Marvel vs Capcom 2 years to become the mythical legend it is. Started in arcade, then ported over to Dreamcast, PS2, Xbox. It’s not gonna happen overnight. And I love Tokon, I want more of it. We need to really end the stupid seasonal DLC crap. Just launch with more characters,” another said.

The FGC culture is so different than I remember. Marvel Tokon came out August 6th. Not even two months ago. Not… even… two months ago. I’ve seen such an insane amount of doom posting for a fighting game that has not even been able to breath for two months lol — Mightykeef (@MightyKeef) September 23, 2026

The FGC culture is so different than I remember. Marvel Tokon came out August 6th. Not even two months ago. Not… even… two months ago. I’ve seen such an insane amount of doom posting for a fighting game that has not even been able to breath for two months lol

What’s your take on this conversation? Do you think Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is in a healthy state with a bright future ahead, or do you believe that the game is already on its way to irrelevance? Let us know in the comments below.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Save Over 50% Off One of the Coolest Desktop Charging Stations I've Ever Seen
articles.summary: Features three AC outlets and four USB-C ports with up to 240W of maximum power output.
articles.body:
Tired of the same old black or white power strip? If you're looking for something with no lack of style, then check out this head turner from Mfish. For a limited time, Amazon is offering Amazon Prime members the Mfish E-Tank 240W Desktop Charging Station for $68.17 with free shipping after coupon code " SGH3OZJY ", a 52% drop from its $140 list price. I actually own one myself. It's really well built and is definitely the coolest looking power strip I've seen personally.

52% Off the mfish E-Tank 240W Power Station

Mfish E-Tank 240W Desktop Charging Station

The Mfish E-Rhino power station deserves to sit on top of your desk in plain site. It features a two tone black and silver colorway with three illuminated ringed power outlets. The lights can be rotated through seven different colors and ten different modes. They also aren't distractingly bright. The power strip itself is pretty compact, measuring 7.7" x 2.8" x 3.4", but it weighs over two pounds so that it will stay in place.

Total outputs include three standard 3-prong AC outlets rated for up to 1,250W each and four USB-C ports with 240W maximum power output (140W max for a single port). The cord is five feet long and features a slim right angle plug so you can fit it discreetly behind your desk.

Eric Song is the IGN commerce manager in charge of finding the best gaming and tech deals every day. When Eric isn't hunting for deals for other people at work, he's hunting for deals for himself during his free time.

articles.summary: In this Silent Hill: Townfall puzzle solution video, we show you how to examine and X-ray your patient at the start of Part 3. This involves moving around a scanner and reading the computer to understand how to read your patient's vitals and take a proper X-ray of the chest and skull.0:00 - Beginning00:07 Use the computer to understand how to read each of the three vitals00:21 Look at the systolic/diastolic blood pressure (70/40)00:35 Use the computer, then look at the pulse that fits that range (162 bpm)01:02 Use the computer once more, and then look at the blood oxygen level that fits that range (80% SpO2)02:08 Use the code from your beeper to open the X-ray room (7103)02:30 Line up and ALIGN the skull first, so line up the four white dots in the four white squares near the skull03:01 Look up the values for the skull X-ray on the computer in the X-Ray Dosage Table03:20 Set the machine for the skull X-ray (3 kV, 7 mA, 1 time)04:04 The X-ray button will blink in green if you correctly input all the values04:20 Now repeat these steps for the chest X-ray, starting with ALIGNING the machine on the chest04:50 Look up values for the chest X-ray on the computer05:10 Set the machine for the chest X-ray (7 kV, 3mA, 1.2 time)05:40 Grab the X-rays and finish up
articles.body:
In this Silent Hill: Townfall puzzle solution video, we show you how to examine and X-ray your patient at the start of Part 3. This involves moving around a scanner and reading the computer to understand how to read your patient's vitals and take a proper X-ray of the chest and skull.

00:07 Use the computer to understand how to read each of the three vitals

00:21 Look at the systolic/diastolic blood pressure (70/40)

00:35 Use the computer, then look at the pulse that fits that range (162 bpm)

01:02 Use the computer once more, and then look at the blood oxygen level that fits that range (80% SpO2)

02:08 Use the code from your beeper to open the X-ray room (7103)

02:30 Line up and ALIGN the skull first, so line up the four white dots in the four white squares near the skull

03:01 Look up the values for the skull X-ray on the computer in the X-Ray Dosage Table

03:20 Set the machine for the skull X-ray (3 kV, 7 mA, 1 time)

04:04 The X-ray button will blink in green if you correctly input all the values

04:20 Now repeat these steps for the chest X-ray, starting with ALIGNING the machine on the chest

04:50 Look up values for the chest X-ray on the computer

05:10 Set the machine for the chest X-ray (7 kV, 3mA, 1.2 time)

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Reacts to Fans Asking for Him to Play the Joker After Primetime Performance Goes Viral
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson’s captivating performance as Chris Hansen in A24’s Primetime has sparked an unexpected trend; fans are now wondering what Pattinson’s take on the Joker would look like.
articles.body:
Robert Pattinson’s captivating performance as Chris Hansen in A24’s Primetime has sparked an unexpected trend; fans are now wondering what Pattinson’s take on the Joker would look like.

The actor’s portrayal of Hansen has received acclaim from both critics and casual audiences alike. IGN’s Siddhant Adlakha scored Primetime a sparkling 9 out of 10 , praising Pattinson for “setting the screen ablaze” with his depiction of a “petulant, paranoid” TV host.

One of his lines from the movie’s trailers has already become a viral meme (“You see how this looks, right?”), and fans just can’t get enough of his chilling stare and near-sociopathic take on Hansen, prompting them to ask the question: “What if he played the Joker?”

In the lead-up to Primetime’s release on September 25, curious Batman fans are hypothetically casting him in James Gunn’s separate DC cinematic universe, wondering what his Hansen-esque Joker would look like, were he able and willing to play the part.

“Really sucks he’s Batman, ‘cause his Joker would’ve been generational,” one fan wrote in a post on X.

“F**k it, let Robert Pattinson play Joker and Batman,” another said , while another mused that the “only bad part about Robert Pattinson being such a good Batman is that he’d make such a good Joker.”

Really sucks he’s Batman cause his Joker would’ve been generational — woop (@woop54) September 16, 2026

Really sucks he’s Batman cause his Joker would’ve been generational

Entertainment Weekly brought up these remarks to Pattinson during a September 2026 interview, who humbly deferred to Barry Keoghan, who’s currently playing the villain in Matt Reeves’ film series.

“Oh, Jesus. I mean, it’s such a great part… but Barry’s the man,” Pattinson told the outlet.

He went on to praise Keoghan’s performance as the iconic DC character, pointing specifically to their shared deleted scene in 2022’s The Batman .

“I loved doing that scene with him so much,” he admitted. “I love Barry, as well. I think he’s such a phenomenal actor. It was so fun doing that stuff with him. But yeah, I want him to do it. I’m much more interested in that.”

Battinson is set to return to the screen in February 2028. Filming is already underway, with fans in Scotland posting photos from the film’s set showing the Batmobile fleeing from Gotham police. Photos hinting at an upgraded batsuit have also been shared online, sparking even more speculation as to what will happen to Bruce Wayne in his next highly-anticipated adventure on the silver screen.

For now, all we know for sure is that Pattinson's next Batman movie will go in a "totally different direction," as told by the actor in an interview earlier this month.

articles.title: Producer of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Movie Reportedly Working on New Silent Hill Film
articles.summary: A new report from The Wall Street Journal states that Roy Lee, who produced Zach Cregger’s hugely-successful Resident Evil movie, is now working on a Silent Hill film.
articles.body:
A new report from The Wall Street Journal states that Roy Lee, who produced Zach Cregger’s hugely-successful Resident Evil movie, is now working on a Silent Hill film.

Roy Lee is a Hollywood legend. The producer has had a hand in some of the most successful movies of the last three decades and has a speciality for adapting pre-existing IP, specifically where horror is concerned.

He began his career with horror hits like The Grudge and The Ring, and went on to produce Zach Cregger’s Barbarian and Weapons 20 years later. Most recently, he helped bring Cregger’s Resident Evil to life, which has become the single most-successful film adaptation of Capcom’s video game series ever and the highest-rated video game movie of all time.

Now, it seems that he’s working on yet another iconic survival horror franchise: Silent Hill.

The Wall Street Journal published a feature about Roy Lee on September 20, where the outlet shed some light on the producer’s upcoming video game-related projects.

According to the article, Lee has a staggering 20 or so movies and television adaptations for video games that are in development or production right now. These include Prime Video’s God of War series , Michael B. Jordan’s Battlefield movie , and, most curiously, “Japanese horror classic Silent Hill.”

The existence of a new Silent Hill movie has not been publicly confirmed at the time of writing this article; however, Konami has been extremely bullish on the franchise as of late, releasing two Silent Hill games in as many years, both of which have been well-received.

Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto also revealed that Konami hopes to release a new game in the series every year as it works to reinvigorate its IPs across the board, including titles like Castlevania. With this in mind, the fact that another Silent Hill movie is getting made so soon after the release of Return to Silent Hill isn’t too surprising… especially given the success of Cregger’s Resident Evil.

Return to Silent Hill , however, was a flop. It’s safe to say that hardcore fans of the franchise hated it, and critics’ opinions weren’t much better. We at IGN scored the movie a five out of 10 , saying in our review that it “isn’t the worst entry in this video game movie series, but it fails to accomplish anything that the source material doesn’t do better.”

For now, fans can remain cautiously optimistic for a better take on Silent Hill now that Lee is reportedly bringing his expertise to the project... though Resident Evil fans have been somewhat divided as to how Cregger handled the source material in his latest movie, particularly its ending .

articles.title: Meta Connect 2026 Live Blog – What's Next for VR?
articles.summary: Just a week after the Steam Frame finally debuted and presented Valve's vision for VR gaming, Meta is getting ready to take the stage at Meta Connect 2026.
articles.body:
Just a week after the Steam Frame presented Valve's vision for VR gaming, Meta is getting ready to take the stage at Meta Connect 2026.

While I don't imagine the Meta Quest 4 will be headlining, there have been a ton of rumors swirling around about its XR 'Phoenix' headset. This would essentially be a VR headset that seems to be more focused on passive entertainment than gaming. The company will also likely have new smart glasses, and will spend a huge amount of time talking about AI.

I'd love to see Meta at least tease a Meta Quest 4. Its current-generation Meta Quest 3 headset is still one of the most cost-effective ways to get into VR. However, because the Quest 3 and 3S haven't gone up in price, it's possible that Meta will avoid even mentioning a next-generation version, due to the cost increases it'd likely have to bear.

If you'd like to watch Meta Connect 2026 keynote yourself, it will be streamed on Meta's website , or on Facebook at 4pm PDT / 7pm EDT on September 29. I will be updating this article live, so if you won't want to watch Zuckerberg talk about AI for an hour, you can just stay tuned here, and I'll do it for you.

7:05pm: After a long speech about how Meta is popular because it believes in people, Zuckerberg has said that the future of that endeavor is in Muse, which is an AI agent. It is cute, though.

7:00pm: The show has begun with a live demo of someone working on code and design documents in a VR space. Then there's a call, with a person popping up in the middle of the screen with some seriously lagging audio. Mark Zuckerberg has taken the stage to talk about the technology that makes 'creating' possible. He says "we at Meta, we're optimists, we believe in the power of people." I just wish he would take those glasses off.

6:58pm: We've now moved from a zoomed-out Meta logo to a zoomed in one with a timer. The show is truly about to begin.

6:50pm: The show officially starts in 10 minutes, and the stream has gone from a still Meta logo to a slightly animated one with ambient music playing in the background. At least Apple's events have a better soundtrack.

6:30pm: We're 30 minutes out, and I'm still hoping Meta at least teases a Quest 4 headset.

6:00pm: If the leaks and rumors are to be believed, the headline device this year is going to be a sort of VR headset, but instead of it being closed off like the Steam Frame or the Meta Quest 3, it'll be worn similarly to regular glasses, but with traditional VR optics built into them. If that's true, I have serious doubts about how Meta would stop light from leaking in.

5:30pm: Meta Connect 2026 officially starts in about an hour and a half. I'm already bracing myself for a heaping of AI features. But, hopefully we'll get some cool hardware too.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Hard Mode Is No Joke — Watch AI-Controlled Orks Wipe the Floor With 2 Developers Playing Space Marines
articles.summary: When developers show off their games, they tend to defeat the enemy AI in spectacular fashion. But that’s exactly the opposite of what happens in the gameplay King Art Games just released for its upcoming real-time strategy game Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4.
articles.body:
When developers show off their games, they tend to defeat the enemy AI in spectacular fashion. But that’s exactly the opposite of what happens in the gameplay King Art Games just released for its upcoming real-time strategy game Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 .

In the video, below, creative director Jan Theysen and senior game designer Elliott Verbiest team up against Hard AI Orks in a 2v2 Team Skirmish PvE battle. These two developers have been at the helm of pretty much all the Dawn of War 4 battlefield report videos released so far. But those previous gameplay videos focus on PvP; this time, Theysen and Verbiest join forces to face the enemy AI — and they decide to go up against hard mode.

The video shows two matches, the first of which goes so spectacularly badly for the poor developers that they suffer defeat in just over four minutes. They declare that a practice round — mere training before the second match, in which the pair promise they're “locked in.” They also increase the number of Victory Points needed to help extend the length of the match... just in case.

Well, that didn’t help either. The brutal, overwhelming Orks stomp all over the Emperor’s finest, delivering the kind of sweeping beatdown befitting of a Waaagh! Theysen and Verbiest do their best to keep pace with capturing points and objectives, but are unable to fend off wave after wave of attacks even with auto reinforce of their units on. Behind in Victory Points and starved of resources, Theysen and Verbiest have to way to generate a response army to fight back when the Orks make a push towards their base.

“I think I have to have a stern word with our coders about the hard mode difficulty,” Theysen jokes as he realises the Space Marines are done for. “I mean it’s supposed to be hard but also the boss is supposed to win!”

“I have no doubt that players will come back to us within like a few weeks of launch and tell us, ‘Actually we've managed to beat this within two days,’ Verbiest adds.

“I’m pretty sure that the people in the comments will discuss our shortcomings!” Theysen concludes.

This second match and the video itself ends unceremoniously: with Theysen hitting the surrender button before the Orks deliver the final blow. “This might be the second loss in a row which tells you two things,” he says. “First of all, we are not that good at our own game. And also the AI is pretty strong.

“This is a surrender. It was an honor playing with you, but we didn't make it. Maybe next time. See you soon. Bye.”

And that’s that. The second match lasted 13 minutes, which is a lot better than the first, but clearly not what Theysen and Verbiest were hoping for. I actually really enjoyed the video, not only because it offers a first look at two-player co-op against the enemy AI, but because it shows how confident the developers are in the game itself. They could have thrown that gameplay out and recorded a new match on normal difficulty, or even tried hard AI again, and again, until they secured a win. But no, they wanted fans to see what Dawn of War 4 looks like as it stands today — warts and all — even if that means the developers aren’t covered in glory in the process.

It seems fans have responded well to the video too. “Pretty cool that you guys showed the defeat and how hard the AI can be. Quite interesting!” one person said in the YouTube comments. “I will never do hard in a Warhammer game Orks just nuke you,” another person, clearly familiar with the way Orks work, offered.

Dawn of War 4 hits PC on December 3, 2026. I think I’m going to stick with normal difficulty!

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Double Fine Founder Tim Schafer Questions Economics of the Game Industry Amid Mass Layoffs and Studio Closures
articles.summary: Double Fine founder Tim Schafer says he no longer “understands the economics” of game development following Xbox’s mass layoffs and industry-wide studio closures.
articles.body:
Double Fine founder Tim Schafer says he no longer “understands the economics” of game development following Xbox’s mass layoffs and industry-wide studio closures.

It’s a rough time to be a game developer. Even if you’re behind some of the year’s most successful releases, you still aren’t safe from the chopping block; for example, staff who worked on Battlefield 6 , which enjoyed a stellar launch last year, were axed after releasing the game to critical acclaim and resounding financial success.

Xbox, one of the biggest publishers and console developers in the business, is also in the midst of a huge restructuring, resulting in thousands of planned layoffs and the divestment of several game studios — studios that have been forced to downsize due to their resulting independent status.

Tim Schafer’s Double Fine was one of the studios that separated from Xbox as a result of its massive internal shuffle. Schafer has made no bones about gritting his teeth and doing everything he can to prevent his company from closing, and his latest remarks are a reflection of that determined attitude in the face of an increasingly inscrutable industry.

“I don’t understand the economics of making games to be honest,” Schafer told the BBC in a September 23 video interview . “I often for years thought I understood them, because there are layoffs, which is bad, and then the people who make games realize, ‘Oh, we need people to make games.’ The executives are like, ‘Oh, we fired everybody, we need some people to make this game,’ they hire them back, and then they… you know.

“So I always assume, ‘Oh, there’ll be this cycle of ups and downs, and ups and downs.’ But it’s been down for like, four years, and I don’t know why. I really don’t, because people are playing games, and people are making money, so I don’t know why there’s a big loss of jobs. I just assume it’s, like, someone is being greedy somewhere. But I hope it is a cycle, and I hope it bounces back.”

Schafer went on to say that the entire industry is volatile across both AAA developers and indie studios, alike, despite the high amount of creativity, ideas, and energy from workers in the space right now.

“I think there’s a lot of life and excitement and creativity in the games industry now, especially in the indie space,” he continued. “I’m not one of those snobs who says only indie games are creative. I think a lot of AAA games do a lot of great creative work.

“It’s just that, it’s been a much more violent place to work in AAA, you know, much more stressful, and your work is often not as rewarded, because you will get laid off as soon as you finish your game. But in indie games, there’s no guarantee of being not… not laid off, but out of money after you ship your game. So, they both have their risks.”

Schafer previously described how he managed to keep Double Fine afloat after its divestment from Xbox in an interview with Bloomberg , where he called the ordeal a “creative awakening" that spurred him ownards rather than making him fold.

"No one puts Double Fine out of business except for me," he said. "[Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s] not going to shoot my dog. I’m going to shoot it. But I’m not going to shoot it, because it’s going to do great. A lot of people want to walk the dog."

Xbox is expected to continue layoffs across its business as part of its ongoing plan to reorganize itself, with the most latest of these affecting Halo Studios. Activision is now leading development for he next Halo game, with Halo Studios relegated to other franchise duties.

Image Credits: Shane Anthony Sinclair/Getty Images

articles.title: Save 40% Off the Sony WH-1000XX "The Collexion" Stainless Steel Noise Canceling Wireless Headphones
articles.body:
Sony's WH-1000 lineup is well-regarded as one of the best wireless noise canceling headphones you can get, with the current generation model being the WH-1000XM6. Perhaps lesser known is that Sony released an even higher end headphone in the lineup earlier this year dubbed the WH-1000XX "The Collexion" . It normally retails for a lofty price of $649, but Secondipity (via eBay) is offering a certified refurbished pair with 2 year Allstate warranty for just $389 with free shipping, or nearly 40% off. According to the reviews from people who have ordered from Secondipity, which is a huge Sony liquidator, the certified refurb headphones are pretty much indistinguishable from brand new.

Over 40% Off the Sony WH-1000XX Noise Canceling Headphones

Certified refurbished with 2 year warranty

Sony WH-1000XX Noise Cancelling Wireless Headphones

The Sony WH-1000XX improves upon the WH-1000XM6 in several ways. The most obvious upgrade is the design and build quality. The 1000XX features a sturdy metal frame that's almost entirely wrapped in hand-brushed stainless steel and vegan leather. Even the buttons are made out of metal. There's very little plastic, especially compared to the 1000XM6. Comfort has been improved here too, with a wider padded headband for more even weight distribution on the head and oversized earcups that are designed to sit around your ears rather than on them.

The 1000XX features custom designed and tuned 30mm carbon composite dynamic drivers paired with Sony's latest Integrated Processor V3. The WH-1000XM6, by the way, is still on the previous generation V2 processor. Updates include support for spatial surround sound, DSEE Ultimate audio upscaling, and Bluetooth 6.0 with Multipoint. The 1000XX also features the HD Noise Cancelling Processor QN3 which manages the twelve-microphone array for voice clarity.

Battery life is solid at up to 24 hours of continuous playback with USB Type-C quick charge that can give you 1.5 hours of playtime after just 5 minutes of charging. Finally, the 1000XX includes a fancy case that features a molded-in handle, making it more practical than the one that comes with the 1000XM6.

At this price, it's also less expensive than buying a new WH-1000XM6.

Eric Song is the IGN commerce manager in charge of finding the best gaming and tech deals every day. When Eric isn't hunting for deals for other people at work, he's hunting for deals for himself during his free time.

articles.title: Artist Behind Pokémon 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR Card Gives Tearful Response to Late Influencer's Heart-Wrenching Final Pack Opening
articles.summary: The artist behind a Pokémon 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card has responded after beloved influencer Avery the Poké Kid pulled the card in his last pack opening before his death from pancreatic cancer.
articles.body:
The artist behind a Pokémon 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card has responded after beloved influencer Avery the Poké Kid pulled the card in his last pack opening before his death from pancreatic cancer.

Avery the Poké Kid was just 12 years old when he died of pancreatic cancer on September 19, 2026. To celebrate his life, the young Pokémon influencer’s parents posted a video showing him opening his very last set of trading card packs from the brand’s recent 30th Anniversary drop.

On the very last pull of his second and final pack, Avery pulled a Jirachi SIR, a major win that caused him to shout in excitement. The heartwarming moment went viral within the Pokémon community and beyond, leaving viewers misty-eyed and sorrowful that such a bright and cheerful voice in the space had been tragically lost at such a young age.

Even the artist of the card, who lives halfway across the globe from Avery’s home in Everett, Washington, saw his viral pull. Speaking on Twitter/X, prolific Pokémon trading card artist Akira Egawa said she was heavily impacted by the video and couldn’t stop crying after watching it.

“I’m so deeply moved. I’m so glad I kept drawing. I’ve honestly been in tears ever since I saw this,” she wrote in one post.

“‘I want my art to bring happiness to people.’ That’s one of the reasons I draw. I’m so glad I put that wish into this piece,” she wrote in another, as a response to the news of Avery’s death.

“I want my art to bring happiness to people.” That’s one of the reasons I draw. I’m so glad I put that wish into this piece. — 江川あきら▽AKIRA EGAWA (@rev_akira) September 23, 2026

“I want my art to bring happiness to people.” That’s one of the reasons I draw. I’m so glad I put that wish into this piece.

I’m so deeply moved. I’m so glad I kept drawing. I’ve honestly been in tears ever since I saw this. — 江川あきら▽AKIRA EGAWA (@rev_akira) September 23, 2026

I’m so deeply moved. I’m so glad I kept drawing. I’ve honestly been in tears ever since I saw this.

Fans were equally moved by her reaction, with many pointing out the poetic lore behind Jirachi in the Pokémon universe.

Jirachi is a Legendary Steel and Psychic Type Pokémon that spends most of its life in hibernation. It only wakes up for seven days every thousand years or so, and is only awakened if you “sing to it in a voice of purity.”

Avery had battled with stage four pancreatoblastoma for over seven years. He became a beloved figure within the Pokémon community during his lifetime, sharing his love for the series’ trading card game to the tune of 313,000 avid followers.

A GoFundMe has been started to help Avery’s family cover medical costs, which has nearly met its goal of $130,000.

Avery’s impact on the Pokémon community cannot be understated; his Instagram account is full of supportive comments from longtime fans and newer viewers alike, who are offering their sympathies and sharing their favorite memories of the young personality.

articles.title: YouTube's New A/B Video Test Feature Is Already Creating Fears Over Weaponized Negativity
articles.summary: YouTube is launching a new feature that allows creators to test different cuts of their own videos, leading fans to worry about weaponized negativity.
articles.body:
YouTube is launching a new feature that allows creators to test different cuts of their own videos, leading fans to worry that it could be used for weaponized negativity.

Earlier today, YouTube unveiled a bunch of new features coming for creators in 2027. One of the most notable new features is an A/B test that allows creators to try out different cuts of their videos, allowing them to experiment with different hooks, pacing, and more. In YouTube's own example, the runtime differs by several minutes across three different cuts being tested, so the difference can be pretty radical.

Some have feared that this may encourage creators to test videos that skew positively or negatively before deciding which one gets the most traffic and using that as the permanent choice. One example provided by someone on X is someone making a YouTube video where they review the upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with a positive and a negative review.

stop guessing what hooks your audience 🎣 with video A/B testing, you can test up to 3 edits of a Short or video simultaneously. review the stats, pick the clear winner, and seamlessly lock it in as your video. launching to select creators in 2027. pic.twitter.com/ne9gDvH2K9 — YouTube Creators (@YouTubeCreators) September 23, 2026

stop guessing what hooks your audience 🎣 with video A/B testing, you can test up to 3 edits of a Short or video simultaneously. review the stats, pick the clear winner, and seamlessly lock it in as your video. launching to select creators in 2027. pic.twitter.com/ne9gDvH2K9

This has also led some to wonder how this might be reflected to viewers. Will some audiences watch completely different videos and be left wondering what others are referring to in the comments or on social media? All in all, the feature poses some flaws, but hopefully YouTube can prevent it from being abused.

Photo by Thomas Trutschel/Photothek via Getty Images

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Warner Bros. Pushes Back DC's Dynamic Duo Film, Gremlins 3 Gets One Year Delay
articles.summary: Warner Bros. has pushed back DC's Dynamic Duo and delayed Gremlins 3 by a whole year.
articles.body:
Warner Bros. has pushed back DC's Dynamic Duo and delayed Gremlins 3 by a whole year.

Warner Bros. is preparing its 2028 slate, which has resulted in a couple of movies shifting their release dates around. An untitled Gremlins film, tentatively referred to as Gremlins 3, was set to release November 2027, but has been delayed a whole year to October 6, 2027. The news was accompanied by a new teaser, showing one of the titular creatures emerging from a backpack while mischeviously exclaiming, "Uh oh!"

The new Gremlins will be directed by Chris Columbus , who wrote the original Gremlins and helmed classic films like Home Alone. Not much is known about the next film in the franchise, but it's a project Columbus has pursued for over a decade. It will likely be a while longer before we get any more meaningful footage, given it's now two years away from hitting theaters.

10.6.28. Only In Theaters. pic.twitter.com/kZVLPrNd12 — Warner Bros. (@warnerbros) September 23, 2026

10.6.28. Only In Theaters. pic.twitter.com/kZVLPrNd12

DC's experimental Robins movie Dynamic Duo, which will follow Dick Grayson and Jason Todd's early adventures , is also moving its date. The film was originally slated for June 2028, but will now open on September 22, 2028. The film is expected to be a hybrid between traditional CG animation, stop motion, and puppetry, giving it a unique visual style. The Batman director Matt Reeves and current DC Studios boss James Gunn will both produce the film.

It seems like this may be DC's attempt at trying to make something similar to the Spider-Verse films, leveraging younger characters with a unique visual style. Whether there's as much interest in an animated Robins project as there was for a character like Spider-Man remains to be seen.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Meta’s New VR Glasses to Entice Casual Viewers With 3D and Full-Frame IMAX
articles.summary: Meta has revealed their new VR Glasses, with an eye (ahem) to enticing casual viewers with full 3D and full-frame IMAX.
articles.body:
Tech companies have gradually invaded the film festival space, but Meta’s secret new project was a perfect fit for this year’s Toronto International Film Festival, both because of its entertainment capabilities, and because it feels straight out of a movie. Not far from where I’d soon watch the new Zack Snyder film , a makeshift gallery played host to covert keynote presentations, each with an audience of one, as a well-dressed entertainment executive showed surprising candor.

“We are… self-aware,” she sighed. A strange way to begin a marketing pitch, but a surprisingly welcome one, as she echoed thoughts that have likely been on the mind of anyone who has thus far rejected the industry’s clunky VR-sphere, and its closed-off headsets akin to ski goggles. The Meta Quest (and like it, the Apple Vision Pro) haven’t exactly pivoted society towards Ready Player One, and perhaps we’re better for it. However, the reveal of Meta’s new entertainment-centric gizmo, Meta VR Glasses, arriving this spring, might just be enough of a departure to entice agonistics like myself, starting with the fact that wearing them doesn’t make you feel like you’re in an episode of Black Mirror.

They are, for all intents and purposes, a pair of slick dark glasses. They still have the noticeable bulge of a VR device, but they’re more along the lines of X-Men’s Cyclops than Johnny Mnemonic . These streamlined shades feature a cable leading to a “puck” the size of an iPhone, a battery-and-computer pack you can place in your pocket or handbag, or clip to your belt. Its 45W fast-charging will probably come in handy, since it only holds enough juice for three hours of continuous playback, but the dangling accessory isn’t too obtrusive a trade-off, given the device’s larger, heavier predecessors. The glasses themselves weigh only about a hundred grams — a quarter of a pound — compared to the five to six hundred grams of the Meta Quest.

The biggest upgrade from the Meta Quest, however, is the complete lack of hand-held controllers and the reliance on physical gestures instead. Apple’s equivalent already has this, but the Meta VR Glasses offer the chance to use these flicks and pinches without feeling like you’re in a Saw trap.

The initial adjustments seem pretty easy, between switchable nose pads of different sizes and lenses you can slide left and right to ensure they’re at the correct distance. There’s no official info on what to do if you wear glasses just yet, but some leaks out there suggest prescription lens capability is the plan. Tiny cameras alongside the glasses' stems capture minor movements, like using your thumb to imitate scrolling on a touch remote, or pinching an invisible button, which in turn trigger and toggle menus affixed to the space around you. The cameras on the front re-create your regular vision, with a bit of a catch. The world around you gets noticeably noisier (as in, filled with digital noise) and the frame rate doesn’t exactly sync up with fluorescent lightbulbs, so you might see a bit of a flicker when looking past the floating UX at actual surfaces.

Navigating the real world will still probably be a challenge, and the tech’s hologram features (and spatial audio) for video calling weren’t part of the demo. However, Meta VR Glasses feel aimed at sitting down to watch movies and TV rather than augmenting reality. With its 5K display made of micro OLED panels, 37 pixels per degree, and Dolby Vision enhancements, you’re getting a pretty high-quality image, and navigating it is gamified too. Once you sync your eye movements to the cursor, simply looking at an app icon will light it up. Just pinch to select. But what about the actual offerings? Well, that’s where things get interesting.

In addition to all your streaming favorites (Prime Video, YouTube, DIRECTV, AMC+, Crunchyroll, Plex, and vitally, Tubi), Meta has teamed up with IMAX to bring the world of full-frame, 1:43:1 IMAX movies to your headset. Currently, this is poised to be the only way to watch something like The Odyssey in its native aspect ratio outside of a handful of cinemas. Sadly, that option wasn’t available during our limited tech demo, but it sets Meta VR Glasses apart even from Blu-ray and UHD, which only expand to the size of your HD television — a paltry 16:9. With films like The Odyssey , Sinners and Dune: Part Three reflecting an increased demand for the format, which can’t fully be met, this is the next best thing.

But what does actually watching a movie in one of these look like? Well, you have a couple of options. For most films, a screen pops up at a certain distance, which you’ll eventually be able to move back or forth. This feature wasn’t yet available, leaving part of the screen outside the glasses’ field of view, which isn’t ideal, but it’s still early days since the product is several months away from release. Your second option, for select films and experiences, is an “Immersive Cinema” virtual reality viewing room by ILM, built in sync with the movie itself. For this Disney+ demo, I picked Avengers: Infinity War — specifically, the scene where Thor harnesses the power of a dying star to forge his new hammer, Stormbreaker. If you’ve ever fantasized about watching a movie while seated in a grungy space factory as lava splashes from around the screen, you’re in luck. For Marvel and Star Wars offerings, environments like Tatooine and Avengers Tower appear to be in the works.

The 3D isn’t too bad either (as evidenced by a short clip of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness), though the effect is no more or less immersive than most current 3D television sets. Upon launch, 3D offerings will be available from the likes of HBO Max, Paramount+ and Peacock. However, where things get really novel is the switch from movies to sports, where you have the option of not just watching your game of choice with a 180-degree field of view — in this case, Game 4 of the 2026 NBA finals; go Knicks — but sitting in a variety of courtside seats and glancing around. This isn’t magic; the folks at Meta had cameras appropriately placed to capture the effect, so future games will have to be equipped for this sort of broadcast if you want to, say, wave at Spike Lee as he jumps around euphorically. Then again, between the NBA finals and the FIFA World Cup, if this summer has proved anything, it’s that sports are a social event, so closing yourself off this way might at best be a backup for plans that fall through.

The speakers on the glasses — which you can control using tiny buttons along the bottoms of the stems — provide a fairly immersive surround sound experience courtesy of Dolby Atmos. This comes in handy for playing music-based games like Beat Saber, one of 75 built-in games available at launch (this particular version was enhanced for the device’s handsfree capabilities) in addition to the XBOX Cloud Gaming, i.e. streaming games directly to your headset. You also have the option of scrolling social media, and typing on a nifty keyboard projected on flat surfaces in front of you, as you look down at your digital ghost hands and their spectral glow. The novelty will probably wear off after a while, but at first, it’s pretty thrilling if you’ve never used this kind of technology before — which appears to be the target market for Meta VR Glasses. Of course, there’s a work capability too; you can mirror your Mac or PC into this virtual space, either wirelessly or via USB-C.

On the other hand, the device’s $1,299.99 price tag — more than a solid TV and Blu-ray player combined — might be a deterrent to the average consumer who hasn’t yet dipped their toe into VR. That is, unless Meta plans to roll out highly involved tech demos for every potential buyer. The only way to be remotely convinced of the technology is to experience it for yourself, which a re-creation on a flat screen (say, a YouTube video) can’t fully convey. There’s a candy store feeling to wearing one of these and turning around to see a fully (or semi) rendered space behind you, waiting to be filled.

There are kinks that still need to be worked out by launch, like the glare from light sources behind you leaking into your field of view (perhaps the one downside to opening up those goggles), but a head tilt here or there can probably solve that issue. Also not part of the tech demo was the ability to re-orient where exactly in your horizontal field of view a given screen appears, but this was something Meta’s engineers demonstrated for us on the fly, with the promise that we’d eventually be able to do it ourselves. Much like legs in the Metaverse, it’s coming, baby.

Look, it can be hard to trust big tech in our increasingly dystopian world, and who knows what data this particular chapter of the company will try to harness or sell. But the lineup of streaming services and viewing features on offer makes Meta VR Glasses one of the more intriguing developments in the field if you’re unsure about stepping into virtual spaces. Compared to existing devices on the market, the openness of the design — which still allows you to peek out from time to time and go back to the real world pretty easily — makes for the kind of compromise that fence-sitters like myself might just be able to accept. If nothing else, it’s more convenient, and slightly less embarrassing, than buying a scalped IMAX ticket on eBay.
